habitats: Leeward alpine gullies below the summit
summary: A 1.5–3 m giant rosette with ascending leaves above a 0.5–1 m caudex insulated by dead foliage. Hairy leaves close around the bud at night and red-purple margins screen radiation. Only leeward gullies support the tallest individuals; windward crater rims and summit crests are excluded (F7, F14, F15, F19, F25).

chains.trait: Insulated short caudex and enclosing leaves
links: High slopes experience cold nights and seasonal snow.
Dead foliage slows heat loss from the short caudex.
Living leaves fold over the bud at night.
Leeward gullies reduce wind exposure enough to support the tallest crowns.
chains.play: Use a sheltered rosette's lee for a brief pause and inspect accessible axils for seasonal water.
chains.weakness: Snow burial, saturated roots and removal of insulating leaves damage the plant.
observe: Inner leaves close over the bud at dusk.
A torn skirt reveals a short caudex.
The tallest crowns occur inside leeward gullies.

plausibility.summary: Caudex height is 0.5–1 m and total height including foliage is 1.5–3 m. Reserve the tallest plants for leeward gullies; exclude windward crater rims and summit crests.

analogues.mechanism: Retained dead foliage and enclosing rosette leaves protect growing tissues against alpine cold.

links: Hairs scatter radiation and shelter leaf surfaces.
Red-purple pigments overlay green tissue and moderate radiation injury.
chains.play: Read exposed purple margins as a cue to high-slope stress.
chains.weakness: Screening reduces useful light and cannot provide a calibrated safe-exposure time.

plausibility.summary: Red-purple colour indicates radiation stress rather than alkaloids in this species. It provides neither healing gel nor dependable creature-sized UV protection.

analogues.mechanism: Foliar pigments can reduce light-induced injury; the combined hairy rosette design is a fictional adaptation.

food_for: High-altitude herbivores browsing outer green leaves

poison.signal: Red-purple margins indicate radiation stress without establishing alkaloid toxicity.

gameplay.cover: Small leeward pocket and partial concealment for a crouching small creature.
gameplay.nest_material: Naturally shed leaves; attached dead foliage remains protective insulation.
gameplay.notes: Axil water is intermittent and not certified potable. Shelter does not provide continuous warmth or reliable UV protection.

relations.note: Browses reachable outer leaves below the protected bud.
Uses firm old-leaf columns as brief perches in sheltered gullies.
May adjoin grass confined to damp protected alpine fissures.

generator.trunk: Unbranched caudex 0.5–1 m high beneath retained dead foliage; ascending blades complete total height.

branching.buttress: None; compact roots anchor in stable soil.

leaf.type: Long hairy tapering blade with flexible base
leaf.arrangement: Dense terminal spiral; inner blades close at night

overlay_rules: Dead skirts turn buff to brown.
Purple does not encode metal contamination.

placement.slope: Stable sheltered alpine ground; tallest instances only in leeward gullies. Exclude active scree, windward crater rims and summit crests.
placement.wetness: Seasonal snowmelt with freely drained roots.
placement.soil: Weathered andesite, volcanic grit and accumulated humus.
placement.fog: Occasional upslope cloud; no persistent fog requirement.
placement.density: Scattered sheltered groups; maximum-height plants restricted to leeward gully interiors.

generator.seasonal: Slow evergreen growth increases after thaw; night closure operates while leaves remain unfrozen.
generator.wind_response: Leaves stream and bend; terrain shelter protects tall crowns, though gales still tear tips.

journal.en: It keeps its old leaves as a coat and folds the living ones over its heart.
journal.es: Guarda las hojas muertas como abrigo y pliega las vivas sobre el corazón.
